preamble: Proto-Semitic had a voiced velar or uvular fricative *ġ [ɣ~ʁ] distinct from the pharyngeal *ʿ [ʕ]. Arabic, Ugaritic and the Old South Arabian script kept them apart, but in Canaanite (including Hebrew) and Aramaic *ġ merged into ʿayin. Greek transcriptions such as Gaza and Gomorrha show that Hebrew still had the velar or uvular sound in the 3rd century BCE; the merger was complete by Tiberian Hebrew.

examples.note: The Greek and Latin spelling with G preserves the older velar or uvular value; Hebrew merged it with ʿayin.
